# local 0002: mcs51 small and medium models: compiler crash for global initializers that need address arithmetic at run time

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17158
- Recommended action: Reject these initializers with error 2 in every model, or give spill locations outside functions a static location.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

Each of the three files below makes `sdcc -mmcs51 -c FILE.c` fail on r17158. The command selects
the small model.

`a.c` gives the internal error of `wassert (currFunc)` in `canOverlayLocals` in `src/SDCCmem.c`,
and then a segmentation fault. With `--stack-auto` it gives a segmentation fault in
`createStackSpil` in `src/mcs51/ralloc.c`.

```c
extern char x, y;
unsigned long long a = (unsigned long long)(unsigned)&x + (unsigned)&y;
```

For `b.c` the compiler writes assembly with a bit named `_(null)_sloc0_1_0`, and the assembler
rejects it.

```c
char x[4];
int c = &x[1] && &x[2];
```

`c.c` gives a segmentation fault in `visit` in `src/SDCClrange.c`.

```c
char x, y;
int a = (&x == &y) ? 1 : 2;
```

The medium model accepts these initializers and fails on them as the small model does. With
`--model-large` the compiler reports error 2, "Initializer element is not a constant expression",
and so do the stm8 and z80 ports.

## Cause

`emitRegularMap` in `src/SDCCglue.c` initializes global variables outside the `xidata` and
`initialized` segments by code. It calls `eBBlockFromiCode (iCodeFromAst (ival))` when
`constExprTree` accepts the initializer, and `currFunc` is NULL during that call. `constExprTree`
accepts the three initializers above.

The mcs51 register allocator spills a temporary in the code for `a.c` and `b.c`. `createStackSpil`
calls `allocLocal` in `src/SDCCmem.c`, which formats `currFunc->name` into the name of the spill
location and puts the location in the overlay segment. `canOverlayLocals` then fails at its
assertion and dereferences `currFunc`. With `--stack-auto`, `createStackSpil` dereferences
`currFunc` itself to enlarge the stack frame.

The crash for `c.c` is a separate defect. In its default case, `visit` advances to `ic->next` and
reads the iCode there without a check. The initialization code ends at that point, and the pointer
is NULL.

## Open

Two fixes are possible. The first rejects these initializers with error 2 in every model. C11 6.6
does not require an implementation to accept them, and the large model rejects them.

The second gives spill locations outside functions a static location with a name of their own.
`emitMaps` emits the `data` and `bit` segments before it calls `emitRegularMap` for `pdata` and
`xdata`, so a location that the initialization code of those segments adds to `data` or `bit` is
not allocated. With this fix `visit` also needs a check for the end of the iCode chain.

## Related

Bug #3895 reports the same assertion for an array with an initializer. That case compiles on
r17158.
